title: Generative AI helped me bridge the gap between engineering and visual production for my iOS game
author: ia-bin
selftext:
Hi everyone — I just released my first iOS game, **iaReveal**.

I come from a more technical/product-development mindset, and one of the biggest challenges for developers like me is that building the game logic and building the visual world are very different skill sets.

Generative AI helped me bridge part of that gap.

For iaReveal, I used AI tools to assist with some **artwork, visual assets, and UI exploration**, while the gameplay mechanics, rules, interaction logic, and core systems were designed and developed by us.

The core idea of the game is simple: **the photo itself becomes the game.**

Players begin with a scrambled image, gradually discover what they’re looking at through gameplay, and finally reveal the complete picture.

What I found especially useful about AI was not that it “designed the game for me,” but that it made visual production more accessible.

For technical developers, especially those with engineering or programming backgrounds, visual production can be one of the biggest barriers between a working prototype and something that feels like a real product.

AI can help with:

* exploring visual directions quickly
* producing draft assets for iteration
* testing UI concepts
* creating variations for different themes
* reducing the time between an idea and something playable

But it still requires a lot of human judgment.

In my case, a beautiful image is not automatically a good gameplay image. The image has to work when fragmented, stay visually readable, create enough mystery, and feel satisfying when fully revealed.

So the process became less about “generate an image” and more about **generate → evaluate → adjust → test in gameplay → repeat**.

I think this is one of the most interesting opportunities for generative AI in indie development: helping technically strong developers cover areas outside their original specialization, without changing who is responsible for the product decisions.

**Play your photos. Challenge your mind. Relive what you love.**
